Aja (West Africa)

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

bafo

  1. corn

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Onomatopoeic. From Old Galician-Portuguese bafo (13th century, Cantigas de Santa Maria). Cognate with Portuguese bafo, Ladino bafo and Spanish vaho.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbafo/ [ˈba.fʊ]
  • Rhymes: -afo
  • Hyphenation: ba‧fo

Noun

[edit]

bafo m (plural bafos)

  1. breath (exhalation)
    • 1370, Ramón Lorenzo, editor, Crónica Troiana:
      Et el deytaua da boca hũa escuma que semellaua chama, et o sseu bafo semellaua que queymaua o ayro.
      He emitted from his mouth a foam that seemed a flame, and his breath appeared to burn the air
  2. bad breath
  3. puff
    • 1390, J. L. Pensado Tomé, editor, Os Miragres de Santiago. Versión gallega del Códice latino del siglo XII atribuido al papa Calisto I, Madrid: C.S.I.C., page 136:
      Et moy rregeo tãgeo o corno que pero que era de marfil que o fendeu cõ o bafo, et al quebrantouselle as veas do pescoço et os nerueos
      And very strongly he blew the horn, but since it was made of ivory he broke it with the puff, and also he broke the veins of the neck and the nerves
  4. vapor, steam
    Synonym: vapor
    • 1409, José Luis Pensado Tomé, editor, Rufus, Jordanus: Tratado de Albeitaria, Santiago de Compostela: Centro Ramón Piñeiro, page 141:
      amasa todo en huun et cozeo en ola noua ben cuberta de huun testo, que non posa ende sayr bafo nen fumo
      knead everything together and cook it in a new pot, well covered by a lid, so that neither steam nor smoke come out
  5. air vent of the oven

Derived terms

[edit]
  • abafante
  • abafar
  • abafo
  • bafarada
  • bafareira
  • bafarida
  • bafento
  • bafexar
  • fedellabafo

  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “bafo”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega

Istriot

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Uncertain. Doria suggests etymology maybe derived from Ancient Greek βᾰφή (băphḗ). Cognate with Italian baffo, Venetan bafo.

Noun

[edit]

bafo m

  1. whisker
  2. moustache

References

[edit]
  • Antonio Pellizzer; Giovanni Pellizzer (1992), Vocabulario del dialetto di Rovigno d'Istria, page 82
  • Sandro Cergna (2015), Vocabolario del dialetto di Valle d'Istria, →ISBN, page 35

Ladino

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

bafo f

  1. breath
  2. blow (act of expelling air from the mouth)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • abafador
  • abafamiento
  • abafar
  • atabafado
  • atabafar
  • atabafo
  • baforada

Macanese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Portuguese bafo (“breath”), of onomatopoeic origin.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈba.fu/

Noun

[edit]

bafo

  1. breathing, respiration
  2. air

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bafo cumprido, bafo di ade (“a person who talks a lot and repetitively”)
  • sai bafo

References

[edit]
  • https://www.macaneselibrary.org/pub/english/uipatua.htm#b

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Onomatopoeic. From Old Galician-Portuguese bafo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈba.fu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈba.fu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈba.fo/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈba.fu/

  • Rhymes: -afu
  • Hyphenation: ba‧fo

Noun

[edit]

bafo m (plural bafos)

  1. bad breath
  2. breath
  3. (Brazil, gay slang) something very good
  4. (Brazil, slang) gossip about news

Derived terms

[edit]
  • abafar
  • bafão
  • bafejar
  • bafômetro
  • bafônico
  • baforar

Descendants

[edit]
  • Macanese: bafo

Further reading

[edit]
  • “bafo”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “bafo”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Venetan

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

bafo m (plural bafi)

  1. whisker
  2. (chiefly in the plural) moustache

West Makian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈba.ɸo/

Verb

[edit]

bafo

  1. (stative) to be alive
  2. (intransitive) to grow

Conjugation

[edit]

animate
